Crazy month as usual. I'll start from yesterday and work backward:

I spent the weekend with David Alan Harvey (Magnum) in his loft in Brooklyn. Reviewing projects (mine and others) and just 'being photographers'. It was a great time. Some other Magnum and NatGeo photographers came by and we went through some first rough edits of their new books, so that was a treat. Michael Christopher Brown showed up and showed his new Cuba project which is amazing. For anyone who thinks an iPhone isn't a camera, I point you in this guys direction who published a few books and is a Magnum photographer...iPhone. Robert Clark stopped by and showed us his Evolution book and Feathers book. You know of him from Friday Night Lights. Peter van Agtmael was there (Magnum). And Teju Cole was there. He's, among other things, the photography critic for NY Times Magazine.

In any case, the weekend was pretty amazing. I showed 2 projects that I'm working on. One on the town of Leadville, Colorado which is the highest town in the US and an old mining town. In 1890 it had 40k people and now only has 1700 registered voters. It's a town that never took advantage of the ski/winter sports here in Colorado but it's changing a bit and I want to photograph it before it gets lost. I walked in and presented this project as kind of a 'recon'. I wanted to get some input on what direction I should take it in, rather than a critique of any of my snapshots. I got some great feedback. Mainly that I needed to up the photo game but that the narrative was great. They told me this wasn't a 'snapshot' story and should be looked at as a bit more and suggested I do the same. They suggested, aesthetically, shooting it on 4x5 or MF. http://imgur.com/a/KmKKb

The second project I showed is a booklet where I take all the hate mail and comments I get from my nude photos and put them together with....nude photos. This went over well. They loved the idea of the project and we worked on editing it down (we took out about 35% and added maybe 5-10% and made it a nice tight edit). NSFW: http://imgur.com/a/8NP1G (note: this is pre-edit. but you get the idea of what they looked at)

here are some photos/snaps from the weekend: http://imgur.com/a/S3mVB and https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T0cmvwwn0xE

In any case, I wish I can actually post more photos and video from the weekend, but I can't :( Anything else would be far too incriminating.

OH, also, one person got a book deal over the weekend to be published by Burn. http://www.burnmagazine.org/ as a book. guess what? iphone. https://www.lensculture.com/ekin-kucuk

Prior to that, I shot a men's fashion job in NYC that went OK. We had to battle logistics of shooting inside and artificial light last minute (night before) rather than outside and natural, but it worked out. That's the benefits of having a huge team (I think there were 10 people on the team + models) here are some behind the scenes: http://imgur.com/a/nhHMl

I'm traveling like crazy this week so I'm typing this on my only 8hr stretch home (if anyone is in San Diego or D.C. this week, lemme know!)

Prior to that....not much going on in Sept. Not sure if I posted my road trip photos? I went on a 3-4 week road trip to Wyoming, Montana, Alberta, BC, hitting every place along the way so that took up most of my month.
